Lemma
[Hessian of the distance function] 1. ch14:14.17\group ch14-boundary-gradient Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0367 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0368 Under the hypotheses of Lemma 14.16, let $x_0\in \Gamma _\mu $ and let $y_0\in \partial \Omega $ be its nearest boundary point. In principal coordinates at $y_0$, \begin{equation} D^2d(x_0)=\diag \left( \frac{-\kappa _1}{1-\kappa _1d(x_0)},\ldots , \frac{-\kappa _{n-1}}{1-\kappa _{n-1}d(x_0)},0\right). \tag {14.99} \end{equation}
Proof

\sketch Differentiate $Dd(x)=\nu (y(x))$. Formulae (14.95) and (14.97) give the tangential diagonal entries; $|Dd|=1$ gives all mixed and normal entries.

□
